The goal was credited to Davies, who was pretty unapologetic about it.The Charlton manager, Nathan Jones, made wholesale changes to his preferred lineup – 10 in total from Saturday’s win at West Ham – and it was a difficult evening for his team. “Absolutely disastrous,” as he put it. “This was a game we didn’t need.” Charlton did enjoy the last word when another substitute, Lloyd Jones, headed home from a corner.View image in fullscreenMikey Moore of Tottenham Hotspur scored their first goal.Photograph: Elli Birch/IPS/ShutterstockThe major take-away was the sense of possibility brought by Sávio, with De Zerbi insisting he was not daunted by being drawn to face Liverpool at Anfield in the next round. “It’s a great game,” he said. “If we want to win the competition, we have to win these games.”It was a night when there was a focus on De Zerbi’s selection. There was a sense of the calvary returning. The manager started Destiny Udogie, Rodrigo Bentancur, Mateus Fernandes and Solanke, players that were fit enough only for the bench at Brentford. Pedro Porro and Micky van de Ven, who did not kick a ball in pre-season and were not available for Brentford, were among the substitutes. They got on. There was no Marcos Senesi or Sandro Tonali in the squad. They will be ready for Newcastle here on Saturday.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideCarabao Cup: Bradford stun Burnley, plus third-round drawShowBradford City extended Burnley’s uncomfortable start to the season with a 4-2 penalty shootout victory in their second-round Carabao Cup tie. Bantams keeper Jon McCracken [pictured] saved from Jacob Bruun Larsen after Zeki Amdouni had hit the post with Burnley's first spot-kick.Both teams missed chances to win the game inside 90 minutes as it ended goalless. The Burnley head coach, Nicky Hayen, made nine changes from Sunday's defeat to West Brom, but the visitors could not break down the Bradford defence, which has now kept four clean sheets in a row.The 2013 League Cup finalists and current League One leaders will face another third-tier side, Leyton Orient, away from home in the last 32. Standout third-round ties include Liverpool v Tottenham, Ipswich v Arsenal, Manchester United v Brighton, Coventry v Aston Villa and holders Manchester City v Norwich.Third-round drawCrystal Palace v MiddlesbroughManchester United v BrightonManchester City v NorwichSunderland v HullIpswich v ArsenalCoventry v Aston VillaBournemouth v LincolnLiverpool v TottenhamChelsea or Luton v LeedsMillwall v NewcastleFleetwood v Sheffield UnitedEverton v WolvesLeyton Orient v BradfordReading v BrentfordPeterborough v BarnsleyWest Ham v Fulham or AFC WimbledonTies to be played in weeks commencing 7 and 14 SeptPhotograph: Sean Chandler/Shutterstock EditorialWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Spurs were always going to dominate the ball. The question concerned what they could create with it. The answer at the outset was very little. Spurs did not threaten until the 30th minute when Solanke had a shot blocked and Archie Gray extended the goalkeeper, Tiernan Brooks, with a low prod on the rebound. Charlton might have been in front by then. Greg Docherty exploded a drive through a crowd that Antonin Kinsky did well to save while Nathan Asiimwe headed narrowly off target.Spurs upped the tempo after the Brooks save from Gray. Fernandes impressed. There was a flicker from Moore, even if the end product was not there. Then it was. Gloriously. When Moore moved inside from the right, the Charlton player close to him – Millenic Alli – slipped. Moore knew what he had to do and the sweetness of the left-footed connection took the breath. The shot ripped through the hands of Brooks.View image in fullscreenDominic Solanke displays textbook technique to double Tottenham’s advantage.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesWhat Charlton did not need shortly afterwards was hesitant defending inside their box on a bouncing ball. Lucas Bergvall saw a shot blocked and Timothy Ouma seemed to freeze. When it broke for Solanke, he swept a clinical finish into the bottom corner.Moore’s only other goal for Spurs was against Elfsborg in the Europa League in January 2025. After that game, his teammate, James Maddison, compared him to Neymar. Moore’s career trajectory has not been as steep as once envisaged but he remains young. He wanted to do more in the second half and there was a swagger about him on the ball; some lovely skills and darting runs. The home crowd saluted him. He remains a loan target for FC Köln before the transfer window shuts. As De Zerbi acknowledged, he needs regular football.De Zerbi introduced Porro, van de Ven and Danso after Gray had once again worked Brooks. It was some entrance from Danso, his first touch a header past Brooks from Fernandes’ free-kick. He was bloodied into the bargain, caught in the aerial challenge by the Charlton substitute, Danny McNamara. Sávio stood and watched. He was stripped and ready while Danso had treatment. He had to wait. When he got on, he more than made his mark.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupTottenham HotspurCharlton Athleticmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Angel Reese is turning trolls and talk of ‘mebounds’ into fuel for a breakthrough | WNBA | The Guardian
description: The star known as Bayou Barbie is shining in Atlanta. The longer her haters dwell on her lowlights, the more they miss her transformation into an all-around force
Author: Andrew Lawrence
Headline: The star known as Bayou Barbie is shining in Atlanta. The longer her haters dwell on her lowlights, the more they miss her transformation into an all-around force
Content: Angel Reese is having a career-best season with the Atlanta Dream.Photograph: Brynn Anderson/APView image in fullscreenAngel Reese is having a career-best season with the Atlanta Dream.Photograph: Brynn Anderson/APWNBAAngel Reese is turning trolls and talk of ‘mebounds’ into fuel for a breakthroughThe star known as Bayou Barbie is shining in Atlanta. The longer her haters dwell on her lowlights, the more they miss her transformation into an all-around forceAndrew LawrenceWed 26 Aug 2026 06.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 06.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOn 16 August, theAtlanta Dreamfaced the Indiana Fever in the WNBA’s showcase matchup, and Angel Reese had a chance to don the cape. Tied at 81, the Dream had possession with five seconds left in regulation when Rhyne Howard launched a deep three-pointer. Reese was perfectly positioned under the basket, snagging Howard’s air ball with an outstretched hand. But in the rush to win the game, Reese forced a shot off the backboard that caromed off the front rim – and Naz Hillmon’s putback fizzled as the buzzer sounded. After Indiana escaped with a 95-91 overtime victory, Reese beat herself up over the loss.“I didn’t sleep,” shetoldreporters days later. “The competitor in me wanted to win that game so bad. I replayed that play so many times.” Reese vowed to shrug the game off and do better. Damned if she hasn’t proved herself to be a woman of her word.Angel Reese breaks two WNBA rebounding records in one night during Dream winRead moreThe past week has been one for the books for the three-time All-Star forward affectionately known as Bayou Barbie. In the Dream’s next game at Las Vegas last Tuesday, she held her own against reigning MVP A’ja Wilson, knocking the defending champions down a peg in the playoff race. Two days later against Los Angeles, she scored 20 points on all nine of her shot attempts in her most efficient game as a pro. Last Saturday against Phoenix, she added a career-high 31 points and 14 rebounds for her 25th double-double of the season, extending the franchise record she set earlier in the month. Reese followed that up by grabbing 26 rebounds – in 40 minutes – when the Dream faced the Sparks again on Monday night, breaking the WNBA’s single-game and single-season records.In a span of four games – all wins, all on the road, all strengthening Atlanta’s chances of locking up the second overall playoff seed behind white-hot Minnesota – Reese has shown herself to be every bit the franchise player the Dream hoped for when theytraded for the third-year vetthis spring. And yet somehow, when it comes to Reese’s reputation on and off the court, there remains this overwhelming reflex to assume the worst.Today’s athletes are quick to call out their “haters” as a source of motivation, distilling the critical noise around them into a broad composite. Reese, however, can actually name screen names. They reliably surface under Dream and WNBA posts touting her on-court accomplishments and in her own social media posts celebratingVogue covers, her customBarbie dolland herinterviewwith Michelle Obama. Piling on Reese has become a sport unto itself, underscored by the stockpile of user-generated clips dedicated to holding her lowlights up for ridicule and scorn. That’s inadditionto the vitriol directed at Reese simply for daring to be a Black female professional athlete in the digital age.These online trolls roast every flubbed layup, every airball, every mental lapse. Most damningly, the internet mob accuses Reese of missing on purpose to pad her own rebounding stats, dismissing her hard-won putbacks as “mebounds”. Even allies like Shaquille O’Neal, a self-appointed father figure, did Reese no favors by suggesting, to her face, that she and her peers would draw more male fans if theylowered the rims and wore hot pants. The trolls were enough to deal with already without Reese’s supposed biggest protector setting screens for them.The vitriol is a relatively recent development in a basketball story that once hewed exclusively to the painted lines. Before Reese was a hater’s delight, she was the Baltimore area’s teen phenom, the beanpole crashing the boards in her mother’s adult rec league, the high school sophomore pushing her team to a state championship. She was the Maryland transfer who led LSU to an NCAA title in 2023 after a procession of decorated recruits failed to get the job done. But of course the problem wasn’t that she won; it was whom she beat and how.Angel Reese highlightsIt was merely Reese’s bad luck that Iowa stood between LSU and the title, and that her testy exchanges with Caitlin Clark would become the spark for a race-based culture war that has only intensified since the two turned pro. The camera crew for this month’s Fever-Dream game couldn’t let the moment pass without searching for anupdated versionof Reese’sring-finger staredownof Clark in the NCAA title game – if only to keep chasing the record-breaking viewership and attendance numbers their matchups routinely command.The WNBA wasn’t the least bit inclined to turn down the temperature when Clark and Reese entered the league as the first and seventh picks in the 2024 draft, respectively. Instead, league promoters pushed their own racial binary, positioning the college rivals as the Bird and Magic for a new era of women’s pro ball. And while Reese has thrived as a basketball influencer for millions of Black women and girls, as likely to turn up atthe Met Galaas ona cereal box(the Allure story on ring-gate leads with Reese’s “black micro-French” manicure), her traditional brand of athlete celebrity pales in comparison to the politically charged horde of casuals that has made Clark the most popular figure in the women’s game.The stakes in this clash were made clear yet again this season when Toronto Tempo coach Sandy Brondello drew a one-game suspension for referring to Reese as a “protected species” – Aussie talk freighted with extra meaning in a country where Reese’s ancestors were regarded as subhuman. (Brondello apologized profusely for the gaffe.) The stark contrast in styles between Clark (the three-point chucker who dazzles the crowd) and Reese (the grinder whose dirty-work contributions are critical but far less conspicuous) only gives the keyboard mob more material to distort.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSign up for WNBA 30: a limited run women’s basketball newsletterRead moreWhen Reese has pointed out, quite rightly, that she played as much a role in building Caitlin Clark lore as anyone, she has risked an avalanche of racist and sexist abuse from online commentators who can barely be bothered to learn the names of Clark’s teammates. “I’ve been attacked so many times, death threats, I’ve been sexualized,” Reesesaidafter the Tigers fell to Clark’s Hawkeyes in the 2024 Elite Eight, bringing a fresh round of social media bile her way. “I’ve been so many things, and I’ve stood strong every single time.” That resilience is hard to miss when she’s diving for loose balls and scrapping for boards.The longer Reese’s detractors dwell on her lowlights, the more they miss what’s happening in plain view: her continued transformation into an all-around force. Her summer move to Atlanta brought about more than a change in scenery. It’s yielded obvious strides in her game. In addition to the rebounding records, Reese is setting personal highs in scoring (16.1 points per game) and total minutes played as her confidence handling the ball, shooting from outside and contesting shots grows. And while Reese still has a way to go before rounding into a rangy frontcourt threat who draws defenders farther from the basket, she has shown herself more than capable of carrying the Dream’s championship hopes on her back.And if the haters are going to keep hating, Reese may as well start beating them to the punch. Last fall, in response to online trolls, she filed a trademark for “mebounds” to make it a slogan for a one-off line of shirts and hats (with the proceeds going toward cyberbullying prevention). If her online trolls insist on spinning everything she does into a spectacle, Reese figures: why try to win hearts and minds when you just can sell tickets? “Whoever came up with the mebounds thing, y’all ate because mebounds, rebounds, crebounds – anything that comes off that board, it’s mine,” she said in aviral post. “And a brand? That’s six figures right there. The trolling? I love when y’all do it because the ideas begood.”Explore more on these topicsWNBAAtlanta DreamBasketballUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Ayyoub Bouaddi: maths student, chess fan and Manchester City’s new Rodri | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: The £85m midfielder passed his exams a year early, is studying for a degree and is ready to tackle Premier League learning curve
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: The £85m midfielder passed his exams a year early, is studying for a degree and is ready to tackle Premier League learning curve
Content: Ayoub Bouaddi is described by a former coach as a ‘very intelligent boy who adapts quickly, capable of playing in every position in the middle’.Photograph: Manchester City FCView image in fullscreenAyoub Bouaddi is described by a former coach as a ‘very intelligent boy who adapts quickly, capable of playing in every position in the middle’.Photograph: Manchester City FCManchester CityAyyoub Bouaddi: maths student, chess fan and Manchester City’s new RodriThe £85m midfielder passed his exams a year early, is studying for a degree and is ready to tackle Premier League learning curveWill UnwinWed 26 Aug 2026 10.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google“He’s like a computer,” the former Lille head of academy recruitment, Mathieu Frison, says of the €100m (£85.7m)Manchester City recruit Ayyoub Bouaddi. “You teach him something, he learns it and can do it immediately.” Bouaddi has the mountainous challenge at his new club of replacing the world’s best central midfielder. It would be difficult for anyone but at 18 it feels monumental, although those who know the Morocco international best would not bet against him.Bouaddi has known onlyLilleand Ligue 1 but is entering one of the biggest clubs in the world where a season without a trophy is deemed a failure. For someone so young, however, he has plenty of experience. He made his European debut three days after his 16th birthday and has played three full seasons in the first team, culminating in a place at the World Cup this summer.Manchester City confirm Bouaddi signing as Marmoush and González head outRead moreAt 13, Lille beat off competition from France’s elite to sign Bouaddi, after showing his parents the pathway he could follow to the first team. There was never lengthy discussion over money, just what would be best for a boy who wanted to reach the highest level. Lille’s track record is impressive, the club bringing through Bouaddi’s soon-to-be Premier League rivals Carlos Baleba and Leny Yoro, among others, in recent times.Frison visited the Bouaddi family in Creil, an hour north of Paris, to explain why a move to Lille would be beneficial after scouts spotted Bouaddi playing for his home town team in a tournament. “He was not here at the beginning of the meeting with his parents, and he came in the house with the ball on a string,” Frison recalls. “He did a very good trick; he always had this ball in his hand and he always played in his house, so he was already very talented technically.”City have faith in him, although plenty of the expenditure is based on promise rather than a finished article. He is not someone who creates highlight reels, but does the dirty work and plays for the team. Others may have sought someone with more miles in their legs, but Enzo Maresca is rebuilding a midfield for the long term after Rodri’s departure for Barcelona and with a £52m deal agreed for Nico González to join Newcastle. The 23-year-old Elliot Anderson arrived from Nottingham Forest as the first cog in the machine, and Enzo Fernández is also wanted by his former manager at Chelsea.Bouaddi, the only boy of four siblings, passed all his exams a year early, is studying for a mathematics degree remotely and speaks English. He is a deep thinker, someone able to cut out the distractions at home and on the pitch. “On the bus, while everyone is watching YouTube videos or listening to music, he will play chess for one or two hours,” Frison says. “In the evening when all the players played Fifa or were on their phones, he studied mathematics, physics, science. His parents didn’t need to push him to do this – he wanted to learn.”View image in fullscreenAyyoub Bouaddi plays for Morocco after representing France, the country of his birth, up to under-21 level.Photograph: Mauro Pimentel/AFP/Getty ImagesBouaddi represented the country of his birth, France, from under-16 to under-21 and is regarded as a huge loss forLes Bleus. “Bouaddi, for me, is one of the smartest players I’ve known in my coaching career,” says the former France under-18 coach Landry Chauvin, who had Bouaddi in his squad for the Lafarge tournament in Limoges in 2024. “He reminds me a lot of Yoann Gourcuff, who I saw in Rennes a few years ago. As soon as the tournament was over, I toldLes Espoirs[France’s Under-21s] that he should have nothing more to do with me, that he had to continue to progress and go above and beyond.”Rodri has won everything worth winning over the past decade while Bouaddi was growing up. Emulating the Spaniard will not be straightforward for a player who is a long way from being fully developed. “When Maresca asks him to do something tactically, he knows that 100% Ayyoub will take the best position for the team,” Frison says.View image in fullscreenAyyoub Bouaddi celebrates Lille’s Champions League victory over Real Madrid on his 17th birthday.Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters“He will respect the game model with intensity, even when he is tired; he will respect the process. Everyone wants a player who can make the difference individually because they can help you to win the game but you need reliable players who you can trust 100% during 60 games of the season. And Ayyoub, he’s this kind of player.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenAyyoub Bouaddi and his family chose Lille because of the pathway to the first team.Photograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty ImagesBouaddi has consistently mixed with – and surpassed – older players, quickly improving as he rapidly went through each step to the top. He was 16 when he featured for Chauvin’s France Under-18s and on his 17th birthday he faced Real Madrid in the Champions League, playing 90 minutes in a 1-0 win against Jude Bellingham et al.“A very intelligent boy who adapts quickly, capable of playing in every position in the middle, capable of evolving in a changing environment, permanently working hard, but also always with his head held high,” Chauvin says. “He has the ability to scan the actions very quickly, to take the information before the others. Very comfortable technically, he always has the right position on the field. And on top of that, he’s a boy who’s charming in everyday life; very respectful, very well educated, who knows all the rules.“The man who hides behind the footballer is simply a very beautiful person. Every time I went to Lille, I would send him a little text, and immediately he came to greet me, even though he was already a pro. Many in his place would have snubbed the under-18 coach, but not Ayyoub.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CityLillefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Chicago Sky ban Enes Kanter Freedom from home games, calling him ‘a potential threat’ | Chicago Sky | The Guardian
description: The Chicago Sky have banned Enes Kanter Freedom from their home games after the former NBA center was ejected from Sunday’s loss to the Indiana Fever
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Chicago Sky have banned Enes Kanter Freedom from their home games after the former NBA center was ejected from Sunday’s loss to the Indiana Fever
Content: Enes Kanter Freedom made a spectacle of himself during Sunday’s game between the Indiana Fever and Chicago Sky.Photograph: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenEnes Kanter Freedom made a spectacle of himself during Sunday’s game between the Indiana Fever and Chicago Sky.Photograph: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/ShutterstockChicago SkyChicago Sky ban Enes Kanter Freedom from home games, calling him ‘a potential threat’Former NBA center barred from Sky home gamesFreedom was ejected after confrontation with CloudOwner says Kanter intended to ‘be provocative’Opinion: Kanter is using his freedom to punch downAssociated PressWed 26 Aug 2026 01.04 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 09.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Chicago Sky have banned Enes Kanter Freedom from their home games after the former NBA center was ejected from Sunday’s loss to theIndiana Fever.Owner Michael Alter made the announcement in a rare news conference on Tuesday. Alter told reporters Freedom is not allowed inside of Wintrust Arena for Sky games “unless sometime in the future he’s able to prove to us to our satisfaction that he is able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat”.The 6ft 10in, 250lb Freedom was removed from Sunday’s game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.I once saw Enes Kanter speak truth to power. Now he only punches down | Bryan Armen GrahamRead moreFreedom was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read “WOMAN noun. adult human female.”The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then did a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Freedom’s direction.Cloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Freedom, 34, as she approached him. A standing Freedom held his arms out and stepped onto the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved in between the two.“It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and just see how much attention he could get and stir up and create,” Alter told reporters.Freedom stopped near the basket to plead his case to security as he was escorted from the court area. He spun around while holding his shirt out and encouraged the crowd to respond as he walked toward the front lobby.He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing the arena.“I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN!” Freedom wrote on social media . “Let that sink in, AMERICA!”Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. But a person familiar with the decision told the AP on Monday that they are not eligible. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the situation.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women – people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity – should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.Although the league’s collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.Also Tuesday, Alter said the team has reviewed what happenedwhen multiple sex toys were thrown onto the courtduring a 73-70 victory over Golden State on Friday night.“We know who the people are,” Alter said. “We saw them, but we don’t have their names yet. We’re trying to get their names. We know how they exited, so we’re going to address that to make that more difficult.”Explore more on these topicsChicago SkyWNBABasketballIndiana FeverShareReuse this content

title: Olivia Moultrie’s injury leaves the USWNT with a thinning midfield pool ahead of the World Cup | USA women's football team | The Guardian
description: The Portland Thorns midfielder fills a role few in the US player pool can match, and she’s in a race against time to be fit for Brazil
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: The Portland Thorns midfielder fills a role few in the US player pool can match, and she’s in a race against time to be fit for Brazil
Content: Olivia Moultrie is among the crop of young players breaking through with the USWNT under Emma Hayes.Photograph: Brad Smith/USSF/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenOlivia Moultrie is among the crop of young players breaking through with the USWNT under Emma Hayes.Photograph: Brad Smith/USSF/Getty ImagesUSA women's football teamAnalysisOlivia Moultrie’s injury leaves the USWNT with a thinning midfield pool ahead of the World CupJeff RueterThe Portland Thorns midfielder fills a role few in the US player pool can match, and she’s in a race against time to be fit for BrazilWed 26 Aug 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 10.15 EDTShareOlivia Moultrie is no stranger to setting her own timeline. Half a decade ago, her desire to go pro at age 15 helped change NWSL rules, which previously forbade teams from signing players under 18. The ensuing five years have seen her go from one of the country’s top prospects to a high-level midfielder, a developmental success with the Portland Thorns.Today, Moultrie instead finds herself in a race against time. The 2027 World Cup kicks off in 302 days, and her recovery froma torn ACLsuffered at the start of this month has only just begun. Moultrie may not be among the biggest stars in the United States’ player pool, but her recovery from this injury should be closely monitored. Simply, there are few like-for-like alternatives who operate in possession as tidily and dangerously as she does.In 1,312 NWSL minutes this season, she notched double-digit goal contributions (five goals and assists apiece) for the first time, playing herself into discussions for major year-end honors as part of a Thorns side who have already equalled last year’s win total (11) with nine matches remaining.In the short term, Moultrie’s injury is a major setback for a Portland team aspiring to win their fourth NWSL championship. Her partnership with Jessie Fleming made for one of the league’s most balanced and dependable engine rooms. Often the most advanced midfielder in a trio with Fleming and either Cassandra Bogere or Nina Nijstad, Moultrie served as the heartbeat of the team in possession, among their most relied-upon players for both line-breaking progression and pure chance creation.Here we see where Moultrie sits among all NWSL players in some of those key areas: near top in touches, and among the elite in progressive passes and expected assists.View image in fullscreenIllustration: Catalina Bush/American Soccer AnalysisHer ample professional seasoning at a young age – she has already logged 108 appearances in the NWSL despite being a month shy of 21 – has helped round out her game.While her breakthrough came across multiple positions, increased playing time has made clear that her best work comes as she helps a team go from the heart of the park and into the final third. Her ability to find open space in the most congested part of the pitch is crucial to bypassing teams who try to congest the midfield with personnel, while her tendency to glide from touchline to touchline keeps her involved in buildup when Portland and the USWNT want to find upfield avenues to exploit.She has also worked to cut out the kinds of fouls that young players can be easily baited into making, dropping from 1.32 fouls committed per 90 minutes in 2024 and 1.17 in 2025 to a mere 0.41 per 90 this year. She has also increased her scoring threat, from 0.18 non-penalty expected goals per 90 (per American Soccer Analysis) last season to 0.29 npxG/90 this year.The additional creative responsibility she has been given in Portland has helped her round into a dangerous playmaker, adept at upfield progression, chance creation and forging her own shots.View image in fullscreenIllustration: Catalina Bush/American Soccer AnalysisShe’s become the sort of do-everything midfielder who can work from box to box that the national team has largely missed since Sam Mewis’s abrupt, injury-induced retirement. Moultrie also benefitted from considerable chemistry with projected starter Sam Coffey, having played alongside the now-Manchester City midfielder in Portland for much of their professional careers to date.ACL injuries have a recovery timeline of nine to 12 months, which will put her on a crash course to be ready for the World Cup, set to commence on 24 June in Brazil. Even the short end of that recovery timeline would put her back on the pitch a mere month before squads are due.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThere is no clear replacement. Even arguably the world’s deepest player pool lacks a bounty of all-around midfielders, and most alternatives would require some form of adjustment for Emma Hayes’s team.Perhaps the closest like-for-like would be Lily Yohannes. The 19-year-old has been ever-present since committing her international future to the USWNT in 2024, earning 20 caps and leaving Ajax for Lyonnes last summer. While the move to a European giant has already accelerated her development and she is an incredibly deft technician on the ball, she was a rotational player in her first Première Ligue season. If she’s a regular starter for Jonatan Giráldez when the 2026-27 season kicks off in September, it could make her the best fit to start at her first World Cup.Another alternative is Claire Hutton, the 20-year-old who like Yohannes has emerged under Hayes, winning 20 caps despite only debuting in February 2025. Hutton predominantly operates as a defensive midfielder for Bay FC, and a partnership with Coffey could lead to an empty-bucket scenario leaving both with a lot of midfield ground to pass through to reach the final third. Nonetheless, her increased responsibilities with Bay have furthered her ability to recirculate possession.View image in fullscreenIllustration: Catalina Bush/American Soccer AnalysisThe third obvious alternative is Lindsey Heaps, who left Lyonnes this summer to return to the NWSL with her home-state Denver Summit. The captain is one of the few remaining holdovers from the USWNT’s most recent World Cup title, but has been in and out of Denver’s lineup with swelling in her knee. When fit, Heaps has fared best under Hayes as a second striker, and her struggles to thread needles and play into the final third from a withdrawn position set the USWNT back at the 2023 Women’s World Cup.After a last-16 exit at that tournament, the program’s earliest ouster to date, Hayes was hired to embolden the next generation of players to restore the US to the pinnacle of women’s soccer. While Moultrie is one of the clearest examples of her coach’s efforts paying off, an ill-timed injury risks leaving her on the outside looking in as the team aim for redemption next summer.Explore more on these topicsUSA women's football teamWomen's World CupWomen's World Cup 2027US sportsWomen's footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Barnes settles stormer to hand Jaissle first Newcastle win against West Brom | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Harvey Barnes scored twice off the bench as Newcastle came from behind to win 3-2 against West Brom in the second round of the Carabao Cup
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Harvey Barnes scored twice off the bench as Newcastle came from behind to win 3-2 against West Brom in the second round of the Carabao Cup
Content: Harvey Barnes seals the deal with his second goal on 81 minutes.Photograph: Zach Forster/Sports Press Photo/SPP/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenHarvey Barnes seals the deal with his second goal on 81 minutes.Photograph: Zach Forster/Sports Press Photo/SPP/ShutterstockCarabao CupBarnes settles stormer to hand Jaissle first Newcastle win against West BromLouise TaylorSt James' ParkWed 26 Aug 2026 16.54 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 19.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAround this time last week Matthias Jaissle wore a sorrowful look as he spoke of his “disappointment” at the “negativity” surrounding a transitional young Newcastle side.Fast forward seven days and a team slightly unlucky to have beenheld to a draw at home by Liverpoollast Sunday have now provided Jaissle with his first competitive win since replacing Eddie Howe as head coach. It is safe to say the doubters are being confounded.Manchester City confirm Bouaddi signing as Marmoush and González head outRead moreGranted Newcastle’s passage to the third round of theCarabao Cupand an impending visit to Millwall was not exactly seamless against a very decent West Brom but it appears that Jaissle’s faith is far from groundless.It helps that he has been able to sign the £30m right-back Amar Dedic from Benfica. Dedic, who played for the German at RB Salzburg, shone here with his stellar crosses creating one of Harvey Barnes’s two goals and another for Bazoumana Touré.“West Brom were a strong opponent, they’re brave and I will follow them now but I’m happy,” said Jaissle, who delighted home supporters by engaging in an animated stoppage-time debate with match officials over a disputed free-kick. “Amar joined us late but it’s like he’s been here for years.”Ten minutes before kick-off Nico González, Newcastle’s £52m signing from Manchester City, was introduced to the crowd. As the stadium echoed to chants of “Nico, Nico,” the Spanish holding midfielder beamed broadly.View image in fullscreenHarvey Barnes sweeps the ball home to score Newcastle’s third goal.Photograph: Richard Lee/ShutterstockWhen González’s new head coach first talked to Newcastle executives about succeeding Howe at the end of July, part of their pitch involved a spot of modern Geordie history. Jaissle was shown a video of 300,000 fans packing the city centre as Howe’s team brought the 2025 Carabao Cup back to Tyneside. “They tried to convince me with that footage,” he said. “But it was not needed.”The German’s hopes of lifting the trophy himself next spring were initially dented as West Brom took a 19th-minute lead.With the visiting Ousmane Diakité establishing himself as a key central midfield combatant, the Championship side grew increasingly confident. When they won a free-kick, Isaac Price curled that 25-yard dead ball around the wall and beat Ewen Jaouen at his near post.Jaissle’s second-choice goalkeeper, a 20-year-old Frenchman signed from Ligue 2 Reims, got a hand to the ball and arguably should have saved it. Not that the 2,000 travelling fans perched high in the Leazes End were complaining.James Morrison’s team impressed while winning their first two second-tier games this season and, for a while at least, his fluid version of 4-4-2 confused Newcastle and subdued Nick Woltemade in equal measure.Then the 18-year-old Sean Steur – culpable for conceding the foul for the preceding free-kick – began re-asserting himself in the home anchoring role. The former Ajax midfielder’s fine run and pass permitted Dedic to whip in a brilliant cross that Touré lashed in from close range under considerable pressure from Chris Mepham.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenEwen Jaouen is beaten at his near post by Isaac Price’s free-kick on his Newcastle debut.Photograph: Adam Cook/IPS/ShutterstockAs Jaissle raised a celebratory fist he could reflect that three exciting recent arrivals – Steur, Dedic and Touré – had combined seamlessly for that equaliser. As Touré, a Côte d’Ivoire left winger signed from Hoffenheim to replace Anthony Gordon, celebrated his first goal for Newcastle it appeared that there really might be life at St James’ Park after Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães after all.Touré was replaced by Barnes at the interval and the substitute wasted no time in reminding Jaissle that he is far from a shabby left winger either. Three minutes into the second half Barnes gave Newcastle the lead after pouncing on the fallout from a corner and firing the ball home from close range at the second attempt after his initial shot was blocked.Quick GuideCarabao Cup: Bradford stun Burnley, plus third-round drawShowBradford City extended Burnley’s uncomfortable start to the season with a 4-2 penalty shootout victory in their second-round Carabao Cup tie. Bantams keeper Jon McCracken [pictured] saved from Jacob Bruun Larsen after Zeki Amdouni had hit the post with Burnley's first spot-kick.Both teams missed chances to win the game inside 90 minutes as it ended goalless. The Burnley head coach, Nicky Hayen, made nine changes from Sunday's defeat to West Brom, but the visitors could not break down the Bradford defence, which has now kept four clean sheets in a row.The 2013 League Cup finalists and current League One leaders will face another third-tier side, Leyton Orient, away from home in the last 32. Standout third-round ties include Liverpool v Tottenham, Ipswich v Arsenal, Manchester United v Brighton, Coventry v Aston Villa and holders Manchester City v Norwich.Third-round drawCrystal Palace v MiddlesbroughManchester United v BrightonManchester City v NorwichSunderland v HullIpswich v ArsenalCoventry v Aston VillaBournemouth v LincolnLiverpool v TottenhamChelsea or Luton v LeedsMillwall v NewcastleFleetwood v Sheffield UnitedEverton v WolvesLeyton Orient v BradfordReading v BrentfordPeterborough v BarnsleyWest Ham v Fulham or AFC WimbledonTies to be played in weeks commencing 7 and 14 SeptPhotograph: Sean Chandler/Shutterstock EditorialWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.West Brom’s legs turned a little heavy but they revived when Lewis Hall handled in the area and Price registered his second goal of the night after beating Jaouen from the penalty spot.Extra time beckoned but Barnes was not about to be eclipsed and duly swept another splendid, low Dedic cross beyond Matt Ingram.“We were in the game, pushing Newcastle right to the end,” said Morrison. “We gave them some problems. I had a nice chat with Matthias afterwards; he was very complimentary.”Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupNewcastle UnitedWest Bromwich Albionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Thierno Barry fires hat-trick as ruthless Everton sweep Preston aside | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Thierno Barry scored a hat-trick in Everton’s 4-0 win at Preston in the Carabao Cup second round
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Thierno Barry scored a hat-trick in Everton’s 4-0 win at Preston in the Carabao Cup second round
Content: Thierno Barry celebrates after completing his hat-trick.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenThierno Barry celebrates after completing his hat-trick.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersCarabao CupThierno Barry fires hat-trick as ruthless Everton sweep Preston asideAndy Hunterat DeepdaleWed 26 Aug 2026 16.55 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 19.43 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThierno Barry resembled a striker reborn, and the goalscorer David Moyes desperately needs, as the first hat-trick of hisEvertoncareer plus an assist for new signing Brennan Johnson delivered a resounding win for the Scot on his competitive return to Preston.The France under-21 international scored eight times in a difficult debut season in England but has half that amount two games into this fledgling campaign. Barry followed up hisheader against Crystal Palacewith a poacher’s hat-trick to give Moyes a convincing victory back at the club where he made his name before leaving for Everton in 2002.“Thierno worked with somebody back home in the summer who tried to change his mindset a bit,” said the Everton manager of the 23-year-old’s early season improvement. “He found it difficult last year, as a lot of boys coming in from overseas do, and it can be even worse if you’re a centre forward. Generally, he has been much better since he came back but I would still like more. A couple of his goals were laid on a plate and I want him to score some of the other opportunities he had as well.”Spurs 5-1 Charlton, Newcastle 3-2 West Brom, Preston 0-4 Everton: Carabao Cup – live reactionRead moreBefore the tie Moyes attracted accusations of a lack of ambition – the kind that has contributed to the longest trophy drought in Everton’s history at 31 years – with a spiky response to being asked how important cup competitions are this season. “I’ll ask you the question,” he had replied. “Is winning a cup more important than staying in the Premier League? What would your answer be?” But a club of Everton’s stature should not have to choose between league survival and cup success. Perhaps Moyes’s question was directed towards Everton’s owners, The Friedkin Group, who have so far shown little ambition themselves in this summer’s transfer market. The Scot maintains Everton are short on numbers and quality ahead of Tuesday’s deadline.The Everton manager could not be accused of treating theCarabao Cuplightly on the evidence of his team selection at Deepdale, where only Jarrad Branthwaite and Tyrique George were missing from the side that started on the opening day. Paul Heckingbottom, by contrast, made seven changes from the Preston team beaten by Wolves on Saturday.View image in fullscreenThierno Barry fires Everton into a first-half lead from Vitalii Mykolenko’s square pass.Photograph: James Harrison/Focus Images Ltd/ShutterstockEverton’s approach mirrored Moyes’s intent. The visitors dominated from the start with Preston struggling to establish a foothold. Harrison Armstrong received a warm reception on his return to the club where he spent a fruitful spell on loan last season and, as against Palace, produced another accomplished display. The 19-year-old’s sharp touches and movement, alongside that of Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, stretched the Championship defence repeatedly.Dewsbury-Hall engineered the breakthrough with a beautifully weighted pass over the Preston defence to Vitalii Mykolenko. The Everton left-back’s neat control gave him time to assess his options and he squared for Barry to convert with ease.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideCarabao Cup: Bradford stun Burnley, plus third-round drawShowBradford City extended Burnley’s uncomfortable start to the season with a 4-2 penalty shootout victory in their second-round Carabao Cup tie. Bantams keeper Jon McCracken [pictured] saved from Jacob Bruun Larsen after Zeki Amdouni had hit the post with Burnley's first spot-kick.Both teams missed chances to win the game inside 90 minutes as it ended goalless. The Burnley head coach, Nicky Hayen, made nine changes from Sunday's defeat to West Brom, but the visitors could not break down the Bradford defence, which has now kept four clean sheets in a row.The 2013 League Cup finalists and current League One leaders will face another third-tier side, Leyton Orient, away from home in the last 32. Standout third-round ties include Liverpool v Tottenham, Ipswich v Arsenal, Manchester United v Brighton, Coventry v Aston Villa and holders Manchester City v Norwich.Third-round drawCrystal Palace v MiddlesbroughManchester United v BrightonManchester City v NorwichSunderland v HullIpswich v ArsenalCoventry v Aston VillaBournemouth v LincolnLiverpool v TottenhamChelsea or Luton v LeedsMillwall v NewcastleFleetwood v Sheffield UnitedEverton v WolvesLeyton Orient v BradfordReading v BrentfordPeterborough v BarnsleyWest Ham v Fulham or AFC WimbledonTies to be played in weeks commencing 7 and 14 SeptPhotograph: Sean Chandler/Shutterstock EditorialWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Preston’s threat was virtually non-existent in the first half. There was more aggression and less deference from the home side after the restart but, just as Deepdale found hope, Barry extinguished it with his second of the night. Dewsbury-Hall was again heavily involved as he exchanged passes with Iliman Ndiaye before stinging Lee Nicholls’s palms with an angled drive. The rebound fell kindly for the in-rushing Barry to poke home.Barry completed his hat-trick with a tap-in from Johnson’s selfless cross before returning the favour with a defence-splitting pass that the Everton substitute slid under the exposed Preston keeper. “I loved being back,” said Moyes of his return to Deepdale. No wonder, on this evidence.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupPreston North EndEvertonmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Mbappé hat-trick sinks Real Sociedad after Real Madrid jeered by home fans | La Liga | The Guardian
description: Kylian Mbappé’s hat-trick earned Real Madrid a 4-1 win against Real Sociedad but José Mourinho’s side were jeered on his return to Bernabéu as head coach
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Kylian Mbappé’s hat-trick earned Real Madrid a 4-1 win against Real Sociedad but José Mourinho’s side were jeered on his return to Bernabéu as head coach
Content: One, two, three for Kylian Mbappé against Real Sociedad.Photograph: Cesar Cebolla/PRESSINPHOTO/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenOne, two, three for Kylian Mbappé against Real Sociedad.Photograph: Cesar Cebolla/PRESSINPHOTO/ShutterstockLa LigaMbappé hat-trick sinks Real Sociedad after Real Madrid jeered by home fansReutersWed 26 Aug 2026 17.39 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 19.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKylian Mbappé scored a hat-trick as Real Madrid beat Real Sociedad 4-1 at the Bernabéu on Wednesday ⁠in their first home match since the return of José Mourinho as head coach.Mbappé put Madrid ahead in the 40th minute before Luka Sucic levelled four minutes later, but the ⁠France forward restored the ⁠hosts’ lead on ​the hour. Vinícius Júnior added a third in the 68th minute before Mbappé completed his treble 10 minutes from time.Julián Álvarez walks alone at Atlético in transfer saga with no end – and no winners | Sid LoweRead moreIt was a winning return ⁠to the Bernabéu for Mourinho, more than 13 years after his previous home match in charge of the club, as Madrid recovered from a disjointed first half ⁠with a ruthless display after the break.Madrid were jeered before half-time after a sluggish opening in which they ​looked short of rhythm, careless in possession and ‌vulnerable on the counterattack.“There’s always a sense of justice in the ​boos and the applause, and the odd boo now ‌and then doesn’t do anyone any ‌harm – it helps you grow,” Mourinho said at full time. “We all know the Santiago Bernabéu and just how demanding the fans ‌are here, and I’m very pleased with how my players responded under pressure and put in a great second half, in which we could even have scored more goals.”Real Sociedad carried ‌the sharper threat early on and almost went ahead in the 10th minute when Takefusa Kubo intercepted ‌a loose pass near the edge of the box and slipped in Mikel Oyarzabal, whose close-range effort was kept out by Thibaut Courtois.Quick GuideChampions League: Fenerbahce stun Lyon, Viking march onShowFenerbahceupset Lyon in the Champions League playoffs on Wednesday to advance, whileViking Stavangerjoined fellow Norwegians Bodø/Glimt in the league phase with victory over Dinamo Zagreb.With the teams locked at 1-1 from the first leg in Istanbul a week ago, the Turkish giants opened up a 2-0 lead in the first half of the return fixture in France. Vedat Muriqi and English defender Archie Brown [pictured] were on target for the visitors, with winger Malick Fofana giving Lyon faint hope in the second half.Viking hit back from a goal down on the night against Dinamo Zagreb, winning 3-1 in Norway and 5-3 on aggregate. Albania's Arber Hoxha gave Dinamo an early lead but Zlatko Tripic equalised from the penalty spot just eight minutes later. Two early goals in the second half from Edvin Austbø and Tobias Moi sealed Viking’s progress to their first Champions League group phase.Barnabas Varga scored a double and former Real Madrid forward Luka Jovic added another asAEK Athenscruised into the league phase with a 4-0 thrashing of Levski Sofia. Romania's Razvan Marin added a penalty as the Greeks booked their progress following a 0-0 draw in the first leg in Bulgaria.Panama’s Cristian Martínez scored the extra-time winner forSlovan Bratislavaas they overcame Slovenian champions Celje. After a 1-1 draw in the first leg, Andraz Sporar gave the Slovakians an early lead at Celje but Svit Seslar equalised fom the penalty spot, before Martínez secured a 3-2 aggregate success.AFPChampions League: qualified teams and predicted potsPot 1:Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Internazionale, Manchester City, Arsenal, Barcelona, Atlético Madrid.Pot 2:Dortmund, Roma, Sporting CP, Aston Villa, Porto, Manchester United, Club Brugge, Real Betis, PSV Eindhoven.Pot 3:Feyenoord, Lille, Bodø/Glimt, Napoli, RB Leipzig, Villarreal, Fenerbahce, Shakhtar Donetsk, Galatasaray.Pot 4:Slavia Prague, Slovan Bratislava, Stuttgart, AEK Athens, Lask, Como, Lens, Viking, Sabah.Photograph: AnadoluWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The visitors went close again in the 34th minute, Sergio Gómez flashing a fine volley just wide of the far post, as the Bernabéu crowd began to voice its frustration.Mbappé briefly changed the mood five minutes before half-time with a flash of class. Fede Valverde collected ‌the ball just beyond midfield and split the defence with a superb pass, allowing Mbappé to surge into the box, cut left and lash a shot into the top ​corner.View image in fullscreenJosé Mourinho was in the home dugout at the Bernabéu for the first time in 13 years.Photograph: Diego Souto/Getty ImagesBut Madrid’s defensive uncertainty returned four minutes later. Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen and Álvaro Carreras were all caught out after Job Ochieng latched on to a long ball, his deflected effort falling to Sucic on the right, who had time to steady himself and drill a low shot past Courtois.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMourinho sent on Marc Cucurella at ⁠half-time and Madrid emerged transformed, with Vinícius and Mbappé stretching the visitors ​with direct running and greater intensity.The ​hosts regained the lead on the ​hour when Mbappé and Jude Bellingham exchanged a sharp one-two, leaving the France captain ​free inside the box to ‌beat Álex Remiro ​with a low finish. Eight ​minutes later, Bellingham’s pressing won the ball back near the byline and his low cross gave Vinícius the simplest of tap-ins from close range.Mbappé completed the win in the 80th minute after Vinícius slipped a clever pass behind the defence, the forward lifting a composed chip over Remiro to seal his hat-trick.“This guy is incredible,” Mourinho said of Mbappé. “I see him really hungry to make history withReal Madrid, and I see a team where, despite Kylian being Kylian, it’s hard for me not to talk about the team.”Explore more on these topicsLa LigaReal MadridReal SociedadKylian MbappéEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Chelsea in talks with Martínez’s camp as Aston Villa close on striker Jackson | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: Chelsea have been offered Emiliano Martínez, who could leave Aston Villa with Nicolas Jackson heading the opposite way for £65m
Author: Sam Cunningham
Headline: Chelsea have been offered Emiliano Martínez, who could leave Aston Villa with Nicolas Jackson heading the opposite way for £65m
Content: Emiliano Martínez is vastly experienced and has won trophies with Aston Villa, Arsenal and Argentina.Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEmiliano Martínez is vastly experienced and has won trophies with Aston Villa, Arsenal and Argentina.Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesChelseaChelsea in talks with Martínez’s camp as Aston Villa close on striker JacksonBlues consider making offer for Argentina goalkeeperVilla agree £65m Jackson deal as Watkins nears £50m exitManchester City expected to make bid for FernándezSam Cunningham,Jacob SteinbergandBen FisherWed 26 Aug 2026 17.30 EDTFirst published on Wed 26 Aug 2026 09.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea have been offered Emiliano Martínez and are considering a bid for the goalkeeper. The club are in talks with Martínez’s camp, and are also braced for a bid from Manchester City for the World Cup winner’s Argentina teammate Enzo Fernández.Martínez has told Aston Villa he wants to leave but a move to Juventus collapsed last week after Villa had signed his replacement,Zion Suzuki, from Parma for £30m.Manchester City confirm Bouaddi signing as Marmoush and González head outRead moreGoalkeeper has been a problematic position for Chelsea in recent seasons, with Robert Sánchez mainly the No 1 butprone to mistakes. Mike Penders, 21, is being lined up to become the first-choice, but the Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso, selected Sánchez for Monday’swin against Fulhamwhen two Sánchez errors led to goals.The availability and offer of Martínez has intrigued Chelsea and they are mulling whether it is too good an opportunity to turn down. The 33-year-old is a vastly experienced serial trophy winner. He won the World Cup in 2022 and reached the 2026 final. He also lifted the Europa League with Villa last season and the FA Cup with Arsenal in 2020.Martínez was not in the squad for Villa’sheavy opening-weekend defeat at Brighton. Marco Bizot started in goal with Suzuki on the bench. Martínez joining Chelsea may solve a problem for both clubs.Chelsea and Villa, meanwhile, have agreed a £65m deal for striker Nicolas Jackson to join the Midlands club. The Senegal international was also a target for Atlético Madrid but is poised to join Villa as a replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal for a £50m fee. At the start of pre-season, Villa expected to retain Martínez and Watkins but in recent weeks both signalled a desire to leave; if their departures are finalised, six of Villa’s starting XI from their Europa League triumph in May will no longer be at the club.Villa offered Watkins a new contract but Riyadh-based Al-Hilal pursued a deal after being given encouragement that Watkins was keen on the move. He trained away from the first team as talks intensified.Jackson will be tasked with filling the void left by Watkins, who joined Villa from Brentford for a then club-record £28m in September 2020. The 30-year-old reached double figures for goals in each of his six Premier League seasons at the club.Jackson has been a longstanding target for Villa manager Unai Emery, who worked with the striker – who spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich – at Villarreal. “Unai taught me everything about football,” Jackson said of Emery last year.Villa also want a centre-back and may target West Ham’s Jean-Clair Todibo.Meanwhile, City are expected to make an offer for Fernández. Any deal would leave Chelsea seeking a replacement before Tuesday night’s transfer deadline. Chelsea previouslytold City to pay £120m by 14 Augustor miss out, but the midfielder remains a priority target for City’s manager, Enzo Maresca, who he worked with at Chelsea. Alonso started Reece James and Roméo Lavia in central midfield at Fulham, introducing Fernández from the bench.City continued their midfield rebuild on Wednesday bybuying Ayyoub Bouaddifrom Lille in a €100m (£85.7m) deal and selling Nico González to Newcastle for £52m.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Explore more on these topicsChelseaAston VillaTransfer windownewsShareReuse this content

title: Debutant Malard breaks Chelsea duck after Real Sociedad threaten WCL shock | Women's Champions League | The Guardian
description: Melvine Malard scored twice on her Chelsea debut to set up a 5-2 win against Real Sociedad in the first leg of their Women’s Champions League qualifier
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Melvine Malard scored twice on her Chelsea debut to set up a 5-2 win against Real Sociedad in the first leg of their Women’s Champions League qualifier
Content: Melvine Malard rounds  Real Sociedad’s goalkeeper to put Chelsea 3-2 up.Photograph: Patrick Khachfe/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMelvine Malard rounds  Real Sociedad’s goalkeeper to put Chelsea 3-2 up.Photograph: Patrick Khachfe/Getty ImagesWomen's Champions LeagueDebutant Malard breaks Chelsea duck after Real Sociedad threaten WCL shockThird qualifying round, first leg: Chelsea 5-2 Real SociedadGirma 29, Buurman 54, Malard 67 88, James 74; Marín 7, Marcos 59Suzanne Wrackat Cherry Red Records StadiumWed 26 Aug 2026 15.50 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 19.54 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea’s sluggish start in the first leg of their Champions League qualifier against Real Sociedad will have made far from satisfying viewing for their suspended head coach, Sonia Bompastor, but two goals from the new signing Melvine Malard contributed to a five-goal haul as the Blues came from behind to give themselves a three-goal cushion going into next week’s return fixture.“It was a tough game, a tough first half because Real Sociedad is a really great team but I think we had a good reaction,” said Camille Abily, the assistant coach to Bompastor, who was serving a one match ban followingher red cardin Chelsea’s quarter-final second leg against Arsenal last season. “We were so much better in the second half, there was more space also. It’s a good win – a tough win but a good win.”Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 6: ChelseaRead moreChelsea looked rusty at the Cherry Red Records Stadium, their new home for domestic cup competitions, with WSL fixtures being played at Stamford Bridge. A commercially focused pre-season jaunt to New Zealand and Australia perhaps did not provide the best of preparatory tests prior to this fixture.Their sluggishness was contrasted by Real Sociedad’s sharpness and a confidence that was perhaps delivered by a strong end to their pre-season which included a 1-1 draw with the eight-time European champions OL Lyonnes.View image in fullscreenMelvine Malard (right) is Chelsea’s impact sub off the bench, scoring twice in the second half.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAThe visiting team were tenacious and well organised and opened the scoring in style when a corner was cleared to the edge of the box and the forward Ainhoa Marín, who joined from Deportivo this summer, met it unmarked, sending a looping shot in at the far post.Despite looking far from their best, the home team drew level in the 30th minute, when Katie McCabe’s corner looked to take the smallest of touches off the captain, Naomi Girma, as it was swept in.After the break it was a different story. Chelsea played with an energy that implied they had had the riot act read to them, or read it to themselves. They maintained their momentum despite the visiting team cancelling out Veerle Buurman’s goal from a Lauren James corner that had given them the lead for a brief four minutes.Chelsea were a tad unlucky that Buurman’s precise sliding tackle delivered the ball to the feet of an arriving Cecilia Marcos who fired past Hannah Hampton to pull them back level. The Real Sociedad bench erupted and the goalscorer, who suffered back-to-back anterior cruciate ligament injuries in 2021 and 2023 and only fully rediscovered her form last season, was engulfed by her teammates.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenVeerle Buurman rises highest to put Chelsea 2-1 up in new surroundings at AFC Wimbledon.Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/ReutersExcept Chelsea had a stronger bench, greater experience and exploited the high line of the visitors to far greater effect as legs tired. It took the substitute Malard 12 minutes to make her mark on her Chelsea debut as they kept their momentum despite conceding. The France striker collected Sjoeke Nüsken’s poked through-ball, sat down a defender and waited coolly for the goalkeeper to commit before rolling the ball into the empty net.Bristol City ready to ‘supercharge growth’ and prove women’s clubs can fly soloRead moreJames delivered Chelsea’s fourth and gave them a more comfortable lead when she turned in Ellie Carpenter’s ball from close range. Carpenter delivered similarly for her former Lyonnes teammate Malard to get her second as the clock ticked down to put the hosts a step closer to the league phase.On whether it is an advantage to have these tough competitive games ahead of the start of the new domestic season next week, Abily said: “For sure. We saw we started slow. We started slow, even though we’ve played some friendly games. We also played against the boys last week. It’s not the same though, it’s not competition. It’s important to have this kind of game.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's Champions LeagueWomen's footballChelsea WomenShareReuse this content

title: Ten-man Hearts stun Rapid Vienna in shootout to reach Conference League | Conference League | The Guardian
description: Beau Reus saved two spot-kicks as Hearts advanced to the Conference League’s main phase despite Tomas Magnusson’s red card
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Beau Reus saved two spot-kicks as Hearts advanced to the Conference League’s main phase despite Tomas Magnusson’s red card
Content: Hearts players celebrate with goalkeeper Beau Reus after his saves helped them defeat Rapid Vienna on penalties.Photograph: Christian Hofer/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenHearts players celebrate with goalkeeper Beau Reus after his saves helped them defeat Rapid Vienna on penalties.Photograph: Christian Hofer/ShutterstockConference LeagueTen-man Hearts stun Rapid Vienna in shootout to reach Conference LeaguePlayoff second leg: Rapid 2-2 Hearts (aet, 3-4 on pens)Kara 34, Cvetkovic 119; Kabore 79, Miller 100PA MediaWed 26 Aug 2026 16.16 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 22.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBeau Reus made two penalty saves as heroic Hearts overcame Tomas Magnusson’s red card to pull off a stunning shootout victory away to Rapid Vienna, and book themselves a return to the Conference League’s main phase.Following a 2-2 draw in the first leg at Tynecastle, the Jambos’ European journey looked to be fizzling out when they were reduced to 10 men in the 75th minute of the playoff round second leg, while already trailing to Ercan Kara’s first-half goal.Football Daily | Celtic raise the bar for calamitous capitulations in EuropeRead moreSubstitute Landry Kaboré equalised a few minutes later before Calvin Miller volleyed 10-manHeartsahead in the 10th minute of extra-time. Rapid hit back in the 119th minute, Nenad Cvetkovic’s goal making it 4-4 on aggregate.But Hearts rediscovered their poise to edge the shootout 4-3 and secure what may be their most significant result in Europe for more than two decades. It means they will compete in the Conference League proper for the third time in five seasons.The visitors suffered a blow in the 15th minute when Tom Renaud was carried off after Rapid attacker Petter Dahl fell awkwardly on his leg while being fouled by Jordi Altena. ­Magnusson replaced the Frenchman but Hearts were struggling to get a foothold early on, and the breakthrough came for Rapid in the 34th minute.View image in fullscreenCalvin Miller finishes acrobatically to put Hearts ahead in extra timePhotograph: Lukas Grinaj/SNS GroupDemir’s low shot from the right took a nick off Oisin McEntee and broke kindly to the unmarked Kara, who slotted into the empty net from six yards out. Hearts were almost handed a way back into it when Cláudio Braga seized on a loose pass but his angled shot from inside the box was beaten away by Niklas Hedl.Hearts enjoyed a spell of pressure towards the end of the half, with Josh McPake and McEntee threatening with shots from outside the box. After the break, the Jambos captain, Blair Spittal, volleyed just wide from 20 yards out, before James Wilson and Braga both spurned opportunities.Quick GuideChampions League: Fenerbahce stun Lyon, Viking march onShowFenerbahceupset Lyon in the Champions League playoffs on Wednesday to advance, whileViking Stavangerjoined fellow Norwegians Bodø/Glimt in the league phase with victory over Dinamo Zagreb.With the teams locked at 1-1 from the first leg in Istanbul a week ago, the Turkish giants opened up a 2-0 lead in the first half of the return fixture in France. Vedat Muriqi and English defender Archie Brown [pictured] were on target for the visitors, with winger Malick Fofana giving Lyon faint hope in the second half.Viking hit back from a goal down on the night against Dinamo Zagreb, winning 3-1 in Norway and 5-3 on aggregate. Albania's Arber Hoxha gave Dinamo an early lead but Zlatko Tripic equalised from the penalty spot just eight minutes later. Two early goals in the second half from Edvin Austbø and Tobias Moi sealed Viking’s progress to their first Champions League group phase.Barnabas Varga scored a double and former Real Madrid forward Luka Jovic added another asAEK Athenscruised into the league phase with a 4-0 thrashing of Levski Sofia. Romania's Razvan Marin added a penalty as the Greeks booked their progress following a 0-0 draw in the first leg in Bulgaria.Panama’s Cristian Martínez scored the extra-time winner forSlovan Bratislavaas they overcame Slovenian champions Celje. After a 1-1 draw in the first leg, Andraz Sporar gave the Slovakians an early lead at Celje but Svit Seslar equalised fom the penalty spot, before Martínez secured a 3-2 aggregate success.AFPChampions League: qualified teams and predicted potsPot 1:Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Internazionale, Manchester City, Arsenal, Barcelona, Atlético Madrid.Pot 2:Dortmund, Roma, Sporting CP, Aston Villa, Porto, Manchester United, Club Brugge, Real Betis, PSV Eindhoven.Pot 3:Feyenoord, Lille, Bodø/Glimt, Napoli, RB Leipzig, Villarreal, Fenerbahce, Shakhtar Donetsk, Galatasaray.Pot 4:Slavia Prague, Slovan Bratislava, Stuttgart, AEK Athens, Lask, Como, Lens, Viking, Sabah.Photograph: AnadoluWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Magnusson then sent a close-range header wide from a Spittal free-kick, but the Icelandic midfielder’s night was cut short when he was shown a second yellow card for a trip on Jannes Horn in the 76th minute.Despite the setback, Wouter Vrancken’s side drew level within three minutes, as Kaboré adjusted his body and chested Spittal’s corner into the net at the near post, sending the game to extra time.Remarkably, Hearts went ahead in the 100th minute when Miller acrobatically volleyed in a cross from substitute Rogers Mato. But just as the depleted Jambos looked like hanging on, Cvetkovic knocked in Moulaye Haidara’s cross in the 119th minute to force penalties.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenHearts keeper Beau Reus saves a penalty from Marco Tilio and send his side into the Conference League.Photograph: Christian Hofer/ShutterstockMiller, Altena, Mato and Sabah Kerjota all scored from the spot for Hearts, with McEntee the only Hearts player to miss. Reus saved two kicks, denying Haidara and Marco Tilio to emerge as the hero in Vienna.Victory brought welcome relief for Vrancken after a punishing run of European results, with his side losing 6-0 on aggregate to Sturm Graz in the Champions League qualifiers. Hearts then lost 6-1 in Lisbon and 7-2 on aggregate to Benfica in the Europa League, dropping into the Conference League playoffs as a result.“We played a really bad first half, a little bit similar [to] Benfica. We had a game plan and we didn’t show the guts to follow up,” Vrancken told BBC Scotland. “We were already pretty angry at half-time, and we came out, we did much better. We took the game in our hands, we were dominant.”“They have to learn that they’re a good team, that they’re good players, that they can show it and show the guts every time, every week, every game,” the Belgian added. “Because in the last away games in Europe, you see that they’re a little bit scared to do things, to take risks or to give spaces away.“But the progress of the team is amazing. The team spirit, I saw it from the first session. They want to learn. They wanted to have feedback, they want to go into it and the kind of football we played. This is the result, they get rewarded, and I’m so happy for them.”Explore more on these topicsConference LeagueHeartsRapid ViennanewsShareReuse this content

title: Uefa to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat | Uefa | The Guardian
description: Uefa is to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: Uefa is to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup
Content: Gianni Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal sparked a backlash, including from Uefa.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal sparked a backlash, including from Uefa.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAUefaUefa to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeatUefa has received guarantees after ill-fated Infantino planEuropean sides will go to under-20 Women’s World CupExclusive byNick AmesandMatt HughesWed 26 Aug 2026 07.16 EDTLast modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleUefa is to drop itsthreatened boycottof Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat ofGianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakesin the World Cup.European teams have been cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, afterFifaprovided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.Uefa had threatened the ­boycott after Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal was revealed and ­doubled down after it was ­withdrawn, saying the condition that “such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again” had not been met.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Despite exchanging barbs in ­public, Uefa and Fifa are understood to have been having private ­discussions over the terms of ­removing the ­boycott threat for several weeks, with the European governing body finally ­getting the reassurances it required.When Fifa confirmed its decision to abandon FFE four days after it became public it neglected to pledge that a similar privatisation plan would not be repeated, but it has now done so in private correspondence.The decision to drop the boycott allows England, who named their squad for the under-20 tournament last week, to travel to Poland in time for the opening game against Canada on 5 September. France and Spain had also listed their travelling party in anticipation that the boycott threat would be lifted. Portugal, Italy and the host nation are the other European countries due to compete.View image in fullscreenEngland’s under-20s will travel to the World Cup in Poland.Photograph: Carlos Rodrigues/The FA/Getty ImagesFifa welcomed the end of the boycott , saying: “Fifa is pleased that all qualified teams ‌will be participating in the upcoming Fifa Under-20 Women’s World Cup. Fifa strongly believes that football has the power to unite, even in challenging circumstances, and looks forward to welcoming all teams and players to Poland.”The boycott is yet to be publicly dropped by Uefa, whose executive committee and federation chiefs meet in Monte Carlo on Thursday. The 55 heads of Uefa’s member associations will convene before the Champions League draw during what is traditionally a significant few days in the European football calendar.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionUefa’s position that Infantino must be replaced has not changed and further steps regarding its stance towards the Fifa leadership will also be discussed at the meeting.Italy’s football federation (FIGC) on Wednesday became the latest to publicly withdraw support for Infantino. “This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC’s position … regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the Fifa president concerning the governance and development of international competitions,” it said.There will be relief in some quarters that younger players, in particular, will not become embroiled in the volatile battle for football’s future. But the fact that Fifa has been forced to mitigate for its president’s actions is another humiliation for a persistently scandal-hit organisation.Explore more on these topicsUefaFifaGianni InfantinoFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content
